problem: Step 2 says the mount-point handle is used 'if absent' as one RPC to S. That hedged case would make the first open cost 2 round trips to S, but the answer states 1. A student cannot tell which case the count assumes.
fix: Say plainly: the export's file handle for /export/ravi was already obtained when the file system was mounted, so it is cached. The only RPC to S on the first open is the LOOKUP of notes.txt inside /export/ravi. Hence 1 round trip.

where: Section 1, definitions of name and identifier
problem: Only half of the standard definition of an identifier is given. The usual definition has two conditions: at most one entity per identifier, and at most one identifier per entity.
fix: An identifier is a name that refers to at most one entity, and each entity is referred to by at most one identifier. An inode number is an example.

problem: Saying the NFS v3 server keeps no per-client open or lock state is too strong for locking: file locking in NFS v3 is handled by a separate lock manager protocol that does keep per-client state. Only the core NFS protocol is stateless.
fix: The core NFS v3 protocol is stateless: the server keeps no per-client open or lock state, and its operations are idempotent, so a retry after a lost reply is safe. Locking is delegated to a separate lock manager that does hold state.
